- The raw JCA provider bounded the PBKDF2 iteration count taken from an encoding (org.bouncycastle.pbe.max_iteration_count, default 10,000,000) but not the counts of the legacy PBES1 (PKCS#5 scheme 1) and PKCS#12 PBE families beside it. Their AlgorithmParameters (PKCS12PBE and its OID aliases, PBKDF1) accepted any count, narrowing one beyond the int range with intValue() so that 2^32 arrived as 0, and every Cipher, Mac and SecretKeyFactory derivation ran with whatever count it was given - including a count decoded by another provider's AlgorithmParameters, as when javax.crypto.EncryptedPrivateKeyInfo.getKeySpec() decrypts a PKCS#12 PBE-protected key with BC. As these schemes carry the count in unauthenticated parameters and derive before anything can be checked, a supplied blob could hold a derivation for tens of minutes. The parameter parse now rejects a negative, beyond-int or over-limit count, and the derivations reject a negative or over-limit count, under the same property as PBKDF2. The PKCS#12 key store derives through the same code, so a org.bouncycastle.pkcs12.max_it_count raised above 10,000,000 now needs org.bouncycastle.pbe.max_iteration_count raised with it.

- The ML-DSA public key constructor taking rho and t1 separately checked only for null, so an ML-DSA SubjectPublicKeyInfo in the SEQUENCE { OCTET STRING rho, OCTET STRING t1 } form with a t1 of the wrong length was accepted by PublicKeyFactory and the JCA KeyFactory, unlike the same key in the standard raw encoding. The component constructors for ML-DSA private keys (rho, K, tr, s1, s2, t0, t1, seed) and SLH-DSA private keys (skSeed, prf, pkSeed, pkRoot) likewise accepted components of any length. All three now reject a component whose length does not match the parameter set with an IllegalArgumentException.

- An ML-DSA private key read from a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo carrying the optional publicKey field (RFC 9881 sec. 6) was checked against that public key on t1 alone, so an embedded public key with a different rho was accepted by PrivateKeyFactory and the JCA KeyFactory. The provider's key then returned the input unchanged from getEncoded(), with a public key under which its own signatures do not verify. The MLDSAPrivateKeyParameters constructor taking a public key now compares rho as well, as the ML-KEM one does, so such a key, accepted before, is now rejected in the same way as one with a mismatched t1.

+- An ML-DSA private key given in its expanded form, whether through PrivateKeyFactory, the JCA KeyFactory or the MLDSAPrivateKeyParameters constructor, was not checked for tr matching the public key it encodes. FIPS 204 defines tr as the hash of the public key, so a key with any other tr loads normally but makes signatures which do not verify under its own public key. The constructor now derives tr from rho and t1 and rejects an expanded key whose tr differs with an IllegalArgumentException. Keys given as a seed derive tr themselves and are unaffected.

- The light-weight CryptoProWrapEngine (RFC 4357 sec. 6.3) diversified the key encryption key in the caller's own array, so after init the KeyParameter it was given held the diversified key, and initialising again with the same parameters - to unwrap what had just been wrapped, say - diversified it a second time and used a different key. It also failed with a NullPointerException when given no S-box, although init has a branch for that case. It now diversifies a copy, and given no S-box uses the GOST 28147 engine's default S-box for the diversification, the one the wrap itself then uses. The provider's GOST 28147 key wrap ciphers were unaffected, as they always supply an S-box and build a new KeyParameter on every init.

- A UserKeyingMaterialSpec carrying a KDF salt was accepted by every KeyAgreement that takes one, although only the HKDF based agreements (X25519withSHA256HKDF, X448withSHA512HKDF and the RFC 8418 XDHwithSHA\*HKDF schemes) use a salt: the X9.63 and concatenation KDF agreements for EC, DH and XDH, and the ECGOST VKO agreements, derived their key without it and gave no sign of having done so. A salt given to any agreement whose KDF is not HKDF is now refused at init with an InvalidAlgorithmParameterException.

- The light-weight ConcatenationKDFGenerator (NIST SP 800-56A concatenation KDF) threw NullPointerException from generateBytes when its KDFParameters carried no OtherInfo, although KDFParameters documents the additional input as optional and KDF1 and KDF2 already treated a null one as empty. Every provider key agreement over it that was given no user keying material hit it: ECCDHwithSHA\*CKDF initialised without a UserKeyingMaterialSpec, and ECCDHUwithSHA\*CKDF, ECMQVwithSHA\*CKDF, DHUwithSHA\*CKDF and MQVwithSHA\*CKDF initialised with a DHUParameterSpec or MQVParameterSpec that carried none. The XDH agreements were unaffected, as they substituted an empty value. A null OtherInfo now derives what an empty one does, H(counter || Z), and KDFParameters refuses a null shared secret at construction rather than leaving it to fail inside the KDF.
